official.deadline_note: Deadline for Canadian institutions to apply through the My EduCanada portal and email the completed Management and Accountability Framework. The 2026-2027 application period is now closed and results were communicated to institutions in May 2026; next-cycle dates are not yet published.
official.application_cycle: 2026-2027 cycle; project activities must be completed no later than September 30, 2027
official.status_note: Official page states: "The application period is now closed." Only Canadian post-secondary institutions were eligible to apply on this call; direct applications from individuals are not accepted.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Tuition is not an eligible expense and must be waived by Canadian institutions
official.funding_period: per scholarship: 4 months or one academic term
benefits: $10,200 for 4 months or one academic term for study or research at the college or undergraduate level
$10,200 for 4 months or one academic term for study or research at the graduate level (Master's and PhD)
$14,000 for 5 to 6 months for study or research at the graduate level (Master's and PhD)
$500 per implemented scholarship (where mobility occurs) paid to the Canadian institution to cover administrative costs - not part of the student award
eligibility: Applicant must be a Designated Learning Institution (DLI)
Applicant institution must waive tuition fees for scholarship recipients

Citizen of an eligible country/territory - Asia: Bangladesh, Nepal, Taiwan; Europe: Türkiye, Ukraine; Middle East and North Africa: Algeria, Egypt, Jordan, Morocco, Tunisia; Sub-Saharan Africa: Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal, Tanzania, Uganda
Enrolled full-time at a post-secondary institution in an eligible country/territory
Paying tuition fees to that institution at the time of application and for the full duration of the mobility in Canada
Able to complete all project activities no later than September 30, 2027
Does not hold or have a pending application for Canadian citizenship or permanent residency

Does not already hold another grant or source of funding from Global Affairs Canada (GAC/DFATD) or a Canadian federal granting agency (e.g. NSERC, SSHRC, CIHR); all additional sources of funding must be declared
Not already enrolled in a degree, diploma or certificate program at a Canadian post-secondary institution
requirements: Participating Canadian institution must identify and select eligible participants before submitting its application
Total funding from Global Affairs Canada will not exceed $150,000 per project
Each participating institution must enter into an agreement with its selected students and is responsible for disbursing scholarship funds to them
documents: Privacy Notice Statement for non-Canadian participants, signed by the candidate and dated within the last 6 months, uploaded through the My EduCanada portal
Management and Accountability Framework, emailed to Scholarships-Info-Bourses@international.gc.ca by the application deadline
selection_criteria: Completeness and quality of the Management and Accountability Framework outlining measures and procedures to ensure a fair and transparent selection process for scholarship recipients
Authenticity and maintenance of supporting documentation
Broad representation of eligible countries and territories
coverage: $500 per implemented scholarship (i.e. where mobility occurs) to cover administrative costs of the Canadian institution, including an employer compliance fee paid to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), if applicable
Tuition is not an eligible expense and must be waived by Canadian institutions
application_method: Canadian institutions apply through the My EduCanada portal: sign in or create an account via Global Affairs Canada Single Sign-On, register the institution (account type Institution), select Study in Canada Scholarships and click Apply
Submit one or more individual scholarship nominations through the portal, uploading the signed Privacy Notice Statement
Email the completed Management and Accountability Framework to Scholarships-Info-Bourses@international.gc.ca by the application deadline
Global Affairs Canada communicates successful results to institutions in May 2026 and does not provide feedback on unsuccessful applications
official.application_route: Apply through a Canadian post-secondary institution - direct applications from individuals are not accepted; institutions nominate students via the My EduCanada portal and email the Management and Accountability Framework
official.study_mode: Recipients must be enrolled full-time at a post-secondary institution in an eligible country or territory for the duration of the mobility
official.citizenship_residency: Open only to citizens of the listed eligible countries/territories: Asia (Bangladesh, Nepal, Taiwan); Europe (Türkiye, Ukraine); Middle East and North Africa (Algeria, Egypt, Jordan, Morocco, Tunisia); Sub-Saharan Africa (Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal, Tanzania, Uganda)
official.international_eligibility: Yes, but only for citizens of the 17 listed eligible countries/territories; applicants cannot hold or have applied for Canadian citizenship or permanent residency
official.duration: 4 months or one academic term for college or undergraduate level; 4 months or one academic term or 5 to 6 months for graduate level (Master's and PhD) study or research
official.description: The Study in Canada Scholarships offer Canadian post-secondary institutions the opportunity to host international students from a diverse range of countries and territories for short-term study or research exchanges. Funded by Global Affairs Canada through the Academic Relations program, SICS aims to strengthen and diversify Canada's international linkages and partnerships. From the 2026-2027 cycle, Canadian institutions are responsible for selecting the students they nominate.
official.program_type: Short-term inbound mobility exchange scholarship for study or research at a Canadian post-secondary institution, administered to Canadian institutions only

not_confirmed: living_cost_coverage - the current official page does not itemise what the scholarship amount covers
travel_coverage - the current official page does not itemise travel coverage
verification.notes: Award values ($10,200 / $14,000), eligible expenses, cycle deadline of 11:59 p.m. EDT 31 March 2026 and the now-closed status were confirmed on the EduCanada Study in Canada Scholarships institutional page (date modified 2026-04-20); the scholarships landing page links to it as the featured SICS opportunity.

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply for this scholarship yourself - a Canadian college or university must nominate you, so the real task is getting onto a partner institution's mobility shortlist before its internal deadline (the 2026-2027 round closed to institutions on 31 March 2026). The award is CAD 10,200 for four months or one academic term, or CAD 14,000 for a five-to-six-month graduate exchange, and your Canadian host must waive your tuition for the mobility to work. Only citizens of the 17 listed countries and territories qualify, you must stay enrolled and paying tuition at home throughout, and you cannot hold another Canadian federal grant or Canadian permanent residency or citizenship.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Full-time students at universities in the listed countries whose home institution already runs exchange or mobility agreements with Canadian Designated Learning Institutions.
application_readiness_checklist: Ask your home institution's international office whether it participates in the Study in Canada Scholarships and which Canadian partners it can exchange with
Confirm you can keep paying tuition to your home institution for the whole mobility period - it is a written eligibility rule, not a formality
Audit your other funding: holding a Global Affairs Canada or NSERC/SSHRC/CIHR grant disqualifies you, and all other funding must be declared
Prepare for the signed Privacy Notice Statement to be dated within six months of the institution's submission - sign it late, not early
Check with your coordinator that your exchange can finish before the programme's project end date of 30 September 2027
common_rejection_risks: Nominations move only through Canadian institutions, so students at universities with no Canadian exchange link are screened out before the award is ever assessed
Being enrolled already in a Canadian degree, diploma or certificate programme disqualifies you outright
Holding or having a pending application for Canadian citizenship or permanent residency voids eligibility
Holding another Global Affairs Canada or federal granting-agency grant, or failing to declare other funding, ends the nomination
Institutions are ranked on their Management and Accountability Framework - a weak fairness, documentation or country/gender representation record can sink a whole batch of nominees
No feedback is given on unsuccessful applications, so there is no route to appeal or reargument
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The current official page no longer itemises what the CAD 10,200 or 14,000 award covers, so treat the lump sum as the total and budget separately for anything the host institution does not explicitly absorb; tuition is waived by the host rather than paid by the award.
document_audit: The Privacy Notice Statement must be signed by you personally and dated within the last six months - an out-of-date signature is a hard stop

Only the Privacy Notice Statement is uploaded to the My EduCanada portal; the Management and Accountability Framework goes by separate email to Scholarships-Info-Bourses@international.gc.ca by the same deadline
The host institution signs an agreement with each selected student and disburses funds - the money never comes directly from Global Affairs Canada, so agree payment timing with your coordinator
Every additional source of funding must be declared, including small home-institution grants
alerts: The application period is now closed for the 2026-2027 cycle; the next call's dates have not been published, so confirm participation with your institution well in advance
The published deadline belongs to Canadian institutions, not to students - an institution can only nominate you if it applies and wins project funding
Award values step up at graduate level only for longer stays: CAD 14,000 applies to 5-6 month graduate exchanges, not to a standard one-term undergraduate move
All project activities must be complete no later than 30 September 2027, so late-starting exchanges risk cancellation or funding adjustment
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Student asks the home international office to route them through its Canadian exchange partner; the Canadian institution selects and nominates via the My EduCanada portal with the signed Privacy Notice Statement and emails the Management and Accountability Framework; Global Affairs Canada awards project funding; the institution signs a contribution agreement plus a student agreement and disburses the scholarship.

official.deadline_note: Applicants were split into two groups: students and graduates of universities in Canada and the United States, and Canadians abroad, faced 23 September 2026 at 4:00 PM Eastern Time; students and graduates of universities in other countries faced 19 August 2026 at 4:00 PM Eastern Time. Both reference forms also had to be completed by the same deadline.
official.status_note: Official page states: "Applications for Summer/Fall 2027 are closed." The application runs annually, opening online around June for Summer/Fall admission the following year.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Tuition and fees for the full normal duration of the master's or professional program
benefits: Tuition and fees for the full normal duration of the master's or second-entry professional undergraduate program
A living stipend of $2,300 per month during academic terms
A one-time relocation grant for moving to Montreal
Up to $5,000 for summer initiatives for scholars not pursuing an academic term during the summer
Leadership skills development curriculum with annual summer intensives, bi-weekly seminars, field trips and other events
A matched mentor, executive coach and advisors, plus access to the McCall MacBain House on McGill's downtown campus
Second-year place-based learning trip to another part of Quebec or Canada
Travel costs covered for finalists attending final interviews in Montreal
Up to 30 full scholarships (20 Canadian, 10 international) and up to 100 finalist and regional awards
eligibility: A current student on track to earn your first bachelor's degree by August 2027, OR you earned your first bachelor's degree in the last five years (January 2021 or later), OR you earned your first bachelor's degree more than five years ago and were 30 years or younger on January 1, 2026 - only ONE criterion is required
Meet the minimum degree and language requirements for McGill master's program admission
Applying for Summer/Fall 2027 admission to a full-time master's or second-entry professional undergraduate program at McGill University consisting of 45 credits or more
The program must take place primarily on McGill's downtown or Macdonald campuses
Graduate certificates, executive master's programs (EMBA, IMHL, IMPM), PhDs, part-time programs and joint degree programs are not covered
Scholarship recipients must enrol and study full-time; offers cannot be deferred
requirements: Two reference forms - one academic and one community - completed online by the reference writers before the application deadline
Apply separately to compatible programs at McGill University; finalists must apply to McGill in December even if the program deadline is later

University endorsement required for Canadian current students and recent graduates (2024-2026) and for international applicants who are current students or recent graduates; international applicants who did not attend a Canadian university or a participating university abroad must seek endorsement regardless of graduation year
Information sessions are offered but are not a stated application prerequisite
documents: Completed online McCall MacBain Scholarship application (personal information, activities, short answers and essays)
One-page résumé as a PDF with a minimum font size of 10 and no photos
All university transcripts as PDFs (official or unofficial accepted); transcripts in languages other than English or French must be accompanied by a translation and submitted together as one PDF
Two online reference forms (academic and community), submitted confidentially by the reference writers
Separate application to the intended McGill University program
coverage: Tuition and fees for the full normal duration of the master's or professional program
A living stipend of $2,300 per month during academic terms
A one-time relocation grant for moving to Montreal
Up to $5,000 to pursue meaningful summer initiatives for scholars not pursuing an academic term during the summer
Travel costs for finalists attending final interviews in Montreal
application_method: Register for and attend an information session (optional but recommended)
Submit the online scholarship application at apply.mccallmacbainscholars.org, listing up to five McGill programs of interest
Send the two reference requests through the online application early - reference writers must complete the online forms by the application deadline
Secure a university endorsement where required before submitting
Apply separately to the intended McGill University program by its deadline; finalists must apply to McGill in December even if the program deadline is later
official.application_route: Apply online at apply.mccallmacbainscholars.org, with two online reference forms and (where required) a university endorsement, then apply separately to the McGill program
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship restriction - Canadian applicants (citizens, permanent residents, refugees in Canada) and international applicants (any other nationality) are both eligible, with separate award tiers and endorsement rules
official.international_eligibility: Yes - international applicants may apply; 10 of the up to 30 full scholarships are reserved for international applicants, who receive higher finalist ($20,000 per year, renewable up to 2 years) and regional ($10,000) awards reflecting tuition costs
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Full-time master's programs (45 credits or more) or second-entry professional undergraduate programs (BCL/JD Law, DMD Dentistry, MDCM Medicine) primarily on McGill's downtown or Macdonald campuses; PhDs, graduate certificates, executive programs, part-time and joint programs are excluded
official.duration: Full normal duration of the eligible master's or second-entry professional undergraduate program
official.description: The McCall MacBain Scholarships enable students to pursue a fully funded master's or second-entry professional degree at McGill University while connecting with mentors and participating in an interdisciplinary leadership development curriculum. Canada's first comprehensive leadership-driven scholarships for master's and professional studies, established in 2019, the programme awards up to 30 full scholarships and up to 100 finalist and regional awards each year.
official.program_type: Full graduate scholarship for a full-time master's or second-entry professional undergraduate program at McGill University, combined with an interdisciplinary leadership curriculum
official.english_requirement: Applicants must meet the minimum degree and language requirements for McGill master's program admission; an English proficiency test score is not required with the scholarship application given its earlier deadline, but must be provided to McGill at admission if required. Reference form responses must be written in English or French, and transcripts in languages other than English or French must be accompanied by a translation.

not_confirmed: the monetary amount of the one-time relocation grant - published as a one-time grant without a figure
the exact next-cycle opening date - only stated as applications opening online around June each year
verification.notes: Stipend of $2,300 per month during academic terms, full tuition and fees coverage, relocation grant, $5,000 summer initiatives and the closed 2027-cohort deadlines (19 Aug / 23 Sep 2026, 4:00 PM ET) were confirmed on the programme, apply and FAQ pages of mccallmacbainscholars.org.

applicant_utility.summary: This is McGill's top full-ride: full tuition and fees, a $2,300-per-month stipend during academic terms and a relocation grant, for up to 30 scholars a year of whom 10 are international. The cycle for September 2027 entry closed in August/September 2026, so the practical move now is to prepare for the roughly June reopening rather than look for a late opening. The scholarship application runs 12-15 months before your programme starts and is separate from - and earlier than - your McGill admission application, which finalists must submit in December.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Current students and graduates within five years of their first bachelor's degree with a strong leadership, community and entrepreneurial record who are set on a full-time McGill master's, JD, MD or DMD programme of 45+ credits.
application_readiness_checklist: Work backwards from the international deadline (mid-August in recent cycles) and register your two referees weeks early - their online forms must be in by the same deadline
Check your graduation year against the endorsement rule: recent graduates from universities outside Canada and the partner list need their university's endorsement regardless of when they graduated

Shortlist eligible McGill programmes of 45+ credits on the downtown or Macdonald campuses and confirm each one's own admission deadline - PhDs, certificates, executive and part-time programmes do not qualify
Convert your GPA to a 4.0 scale using McGill's equivalency guidance and merge non-English/French transcripts with their translations into single PDFs
Draft the short-answer and essay components (character limits are strict - 105 characters for short answers, 225-250 words for essays) around concrete leadership and service episodes, not job titles
common_rejection_risks: A reference form submitted late or by email makes the application incomplete - references are accepted only through the online form
Missing the required university endorsement when you graduated recently from a non-partner university abroad
Applying to an ineligible programme (PhD, graduate certificate, executive MBA, part-time or joint degree, or a programme under 45 credits)
Essays that list activities without evidence of actual role, decisions and outcomes - the five criteria are assessed, not your résumé length
Waiting for the McGill admission offer before applying to the scholarship; most people must apply to the scholarship first
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The McGill programme application fee is not covered by the scholarship, the stipend is paid only during academic terms so summer living costs fall on you unless you secure summer initiatives funding, and only one relocation grant is provided for the move to Montreal.
document_audit: Transcripts in other languages must be paired with a translation and merged into a single PDF - loose files are a common slip
The résumé must be one page, PDF, font size 10 or larger, with no photo
Reference responses must be in English or French, and family members, fellow students or friends cannot be referees
Reference forms are confidential - you cannot review them, so brief your referees on the points you want evidenced
Any standardized test score (GRE, GMAT, LSAT, CASPER, DAT) is optional with the scholarship but may still be required by your McGill programme later
alerts: Applicants may apply at most twice since the 2022-2023 cycle; anyone who has accepted a Regional Award or attended final interviews in a previous year cannot re-apply
Scholarship offers cannot be deferred and require full-time enrolment, so a part-time plan forfeits the award
Finalists must apply to McGill in December even if their programme's own deadline is later - missing that window ends the candidacy
Scholars may accept up to $10,000 per year of additional merit-based funding on top of the scholarship, which affects how you stack other offers
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register online at apply.mccallmacbainscholars.org, secure any required university endorsement, have one academic and one community referee submit their online forms by the deadline, then complete the separate McGill programme application (by December at the latest if you reach final interviews in March).
